You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Fed Officials Turn Hawkish Again, CPI May Set September Path; US-Iran Hormuz Stalemate Continues; Nvidia Clarifies Financing Plan, Easing Concerns (August 12, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Fed officials turn hawkish again; tonight’s CPI becomes key basis for September hike pricing
Chicago Fed President Goolsbee emphasized that rapidly rising prices are currently the biggest problem facing the U.S. economy, while the labor market is “ stable but not strong.”
Cleveland Fed President Hammack stated that the Fed may need multiple rate hikes to bring inflation back to the 2% target .
Markets are focused on the U.S. July CPI report due Wednesday evening Beijing time , with expectations of 3.4% YoY headline and 2.5% core; CME data shows roughly equal odds for a September hold versus a hike. Market Impact : Hawkish comments ahead of critical inflation data are pressuring short-end rate-sensitive assets and keeping risk appetite cautious. The CPI outcome will directly influence September policy pricing.
International Commodities
US-Iran maritime conflict escalates; Hormuz Strait stalemate continues
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Rezaei said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen unless the U.S. accepts Iran’s ceasefire conditions (including unfreezing Iranian assets and ending related regional conflicts).
The U.S. military fired a missile at a Panama-flagged cargo ship heading to an Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman; Houthi forces attacked Saudi and Egyptian vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, causing crew fatalities. Market Impact : Geopolitical risk premiums are supporting oil prices, supply disruption concerns persist, and inflation expectations are intertwining with safe-haven demand, increasing near-term commodity volatility.
Macroeconomic Policy
Market sentiment remains pessimistic; historical data points to potential rebound space
The S&P 500 has repeatedly hit new highs, yet shorts outnumbered longs in 20 of the past 25 weeks, with institutional positioning lagging fundamental improvement.
22V Research noted that excessive pessimism has historically foreshadowed positive returns over the following 1–6 months; Wells Fargo’s sentiment indicator is approaching extreme bullish levels that have previously triggered sell signals. Market Impact : The disconnect between sentiment and fundamentals may provide room for a later recovery, but the near term remains constrained by both CPI and geopolitics.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot Gold : Approx. $4,390/oz, +0.52%
Spot Silver : Approx. $65.0/oz, +0.5%
WTI Crude : Approx. $83.9/bbl, +0.96%
Brent Crude : Approx. $85/bbl, +0.67%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : 99.86, +0.05%
Driver Analysis : The US-Iran Hormuz stalemate and Houthi attacks continue to support oil prices and sustain geopolitical risk premiums. Gold is oscillating between inflation-data anticipation and safe-haven demand, while silver is influenced more by its industrial attributes. Hawkish Fed comments are limiting upside for precious metals. Institutional views hold that near-term commodities remain driven by geopolitics and the upcoming CPI; elevated oil prices may reinforce sticky-inflation concerns, creating a linkage of geopolitical tension → oil support → inflation expectations → interest-rate path re-pricing.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approx. $63,765, -0.43%
ETH : Approx. $1,884, +0.45%
Crypto Total Market Cap : Approx. $2.27 trillion, -0.1%
Market Liquidations : 24h total liquidations approx. $171 million, of which long liquidations $125 million
Bitget BTC/ USDT Liquidation Map : BTC currently around $63,711. Dense long liquidations are concentrated near $63,000–$63,500; a break below $63,000 could accelerate long liquidations. Short liquidations cluster in the $64,000–$65,000 zone; a break above $64,000 could trigger successive short covering and push prices higher.
BTC Spot ETF Net Flows : Yesterday net outflow of $145 million; today’s dynamic net outflow $42.4 million
Driver Analysis : Softening equity risk appetite and rising oil prices have heightened inflation concerns, exerting macro pressure on crypto. BTC failed to hold the $64,000 level, while ETH showed relative resilience. Liquidations were dominated by longs, reflecting stop-loss pressure after the upside failed. Institutional consensus points to a range-bound, mildly weak bias, with focus on tonight’s CPI transmission to risk assets and ETF flow changes.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,791.85, -0.34%, second consecutive daily decline
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,728.20, -0.32%
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,445.45, -0.60%, with the tech sector under clear pressure
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : Approx. $217.50, -0.02%
AAPL : Approx. $304.91, -1.09%
MSFT : Approx. $503.81, -0.44%
GOOGL : Approx. $343.80, -3.84%
AMZN : Approx. $272.27, -2.09%
META : Approx. $599.12, +0.71%
TSLA : Approx. $332.81, +0.58%
[...]
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : The Mag 7 showed clear divergence. Google and Amazon led the declines, with Apple and Microsoft also lower; Meta and Tesla closed higher against the trend. Nvidia ’s decline narrowed after Jensen Huang clarified the financing plan. Overall pressure stemmed from the US-Iran stalemate and hawkish Fed comments, as the market shifted from pure AI thematic trading toward re-pricing of capital-expenditure efficiency and macro risks, producing differentiated individual-stock drivers.
[...]
1. Nvidia (NVDA) – Jensen Huang Clarifies Financing Plan, Easing Concerns
[...]
Event Overview : The market had previously misunderstood Nvidia’s potential $500 billion compute financing plan. Jensen Huang clarified on X that support would be capped at no more than 25% of any single project opportunity and would be limited, residual-value-based support intended to supplement rather than replace independent underwriters. The clarification removed uncertainty and caused the 5-year CDS to tighten. Separately, Nvidia is reportedly developing a trillion-parameter open-source model, Nemotron 4, aimed at expanding the open-source ecosystem and driving GPU demand. CME plans to launch GPU compute futures. Market Interpretation : Institutions believe the clarification significantly reduced credit-risk concerns, shifting the narrative from “unlimited exposure” to limited support. Analysts will monitor the actual operation of the financing platform and the pull from the open-source model on the ecosystem. Investment Implications : Near-term sentiment repair is constructive; the medium-term thesis still requires tracking AI capex returns and supply-chain execution.
[...]
2. Google (GOOGL) – Largest Decline Among Mag 7; Capex Efficiency in Focus
[...]
Event Overview : Google shares fell approximately 3.84%, the largest drop among the Mag 7. The market continues to digest earlier capex increases and the pace of AI investment returns. Market Interpretation : Under hawkish macro conditions and geopolitical uncertainty, institutions remain cautious on high-capex tech names, emphasizing the match between cloud growth and investment efficiency. Investment Implications : Watch subsequent earnings for AI revenue contribution and any changes to capex guidance.
[...]
3. Apple (AAPL) – Followed Tech Sector Lower
[...]
Event Overview : Apple declined approximately 1.09%, moving with the broader tech adjustment. Markets continue to assess its positioning within the AI and hardware cycle. Market Interpretation : Relatively defensive but still dragged by sector sentiment; institutions are monitoring the iPhone cycle and services resilience. Investment Implications : As a relatively defensive tech allocation, track new-product launches and AI feature rollout progress.
[...]
4. Meta (META) – Closed Higher Against the Trend
[...]
Event Overview : Meta rose approximately 0.71%, showing relative strength among the Mag 7. Market Interpretation : Institutions may be relatively constructive on advertising and AI efficiency improvements, with some short-term capital returning. Investment Implications : Monitor marginal improvements in the advertising business and AI investment signals.
